source_name: Skupština Crne Gore — Odbor za ekonomiju, finansije i budžet (committee documents)
why_relevant: The Committee for Economy, Finance and Budget is the lead working body for credit institution, payment services, AML and budget/fiscal bills. Its session agendas, izvještaji and amandmani reveal the substantive changes made between the Government's Predlog and the adopted text, plus the timing of plenary scheduling.

source_name: Skupština Crne Gore — official parliament portal (skupstina.me)
why_relevant: Institutional front door: plenary session calendar, press releases on adopted laws, composition of the current saziv and its committees. Useful as a scheduling/pointer layer that tells the collector when a banking or payments bill hits the plenary agenda; the substantive documents live on zakoni.skupstina.me.

source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore — javne rasprave (public consultation feed)
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance is the proponent ministry for credit institutions, payment services, AML/CFT and fiscal legislation. This tagged news feed carries the javni poziv announcements opening each javna rasprava, with the consultation window (typically 20-40 days), the submission address and links to the Nacrt zakona plus obrazloženje. Confirmed live: entries observed for business-registration law amendments (10.08.2026) and budget/fiscal responsibility law (06.08.2026).

source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore — institutional site and document library
why_relevant: Home of the proponent ministry: sub-sections for državni budžet i javni dug, porezi i carine, budžetsko računovodstvo and a general /biblioteka document library where nacrti, izvještaji sa javne rasprave and strategy documents are deposited. The report-back document (izvještaj o sprovedenoj javnoj raspravi) that shows which industry comments were accepted is published here.

source_name: gov.me — dokumenta repository (draft law texts by GUID)
why_relevant: Central government document store where the actual Nacrt/Predlog zakona PDFs live, addressed by UUID. Observed holding 'Nacrt zakona o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o kreditnim institucijama' and consolidated AML/CFT law texts. This is where the primary legal text is obtained once a consultation or session announcement points to it.

source_name: Vlada Crne Gore — saopštenja sa sjednica (cabinet session communiqués)
why_relevant: The Government 'utvrđuje' the Predlog zakona — the decisive step between draft and parliament. Session communiqués name each bill adopted, often together with the izvještaj sa javne rasprave, and are the earliest public signal that a banking/payments text has been finalised and is heading to Skupština.

source_name: Službeni list Crne Gore (Official Gazette) — sluzbenilist.me
why_relevant: The constitutionally mandated publisher of record. Nothing is in force in Montenegro until it appears here; the gazette issue number and date fix the stupanje na snagu (normally the eighth day after publication, unless the law states otherwise) and any prelazne i završne odredbe transposition deadlines. Indispensable for date-accurate compliance timelines.

source_name: Katalog propisa (katalogpropisa.me) — Pravni ekspert d.o.o. Podgorica
why_relevant: Second commercial consolidator of Montenegrin regulations, with a 'Pregled ažuriranih propisa' page listing which acts were updated and when. Useful as a cross-check on amendment detection and for annotated editions of the Zakon o kreditnim institucijama.

source_name: Ministarstvo evropskih poslova — usklađivanje propisa sa pravnom tekovinom EU (tabele usklađenosti)
why_relevant: Article 40 of the Poslovnik Vlade requires every bill submitted to Government to carry an Izjava o usklađenosti plus a Tabela usklađenosti, verified by the Ministry of European Affairs' Odsjek za usklađivanje propisa. These tables map each national article to the specific EU directive/regulation article (CRD VI, CRR III, PSD2/PSD3, AMLD) and state the degree of transposition — the single most precise indicator of what EU acquis a Montenegrin banking or payments bill is implementing.

source_name: Program pristupanja Crne Gore Evropskoj uniji (PPCG) — accession programme, Chapter 4 & 9
why_relevant: The national EU-accession programme sets, per negotiating chapter, the specific laws and bylaws Montenegro commits to adopt and the quarter by which. Chapter 9 (financial services: payment services, capital movement, AML/CFT) and Chapter 4 name the Ministry of Finance, CBCG, Komisija za tržište kapitala and the insurance supervisor as responsible institutions. It is the multi-year deadline backbone behind individual bills.

source_name: eu.me — Montenegro EU integration portal (Ministarstvo evropskih poslova)
why_relevant: Aggregates accession chronology, chapter status and the PPCG documents. Acts as a pointer hub to the negotiating structures and to which institution owns each financial-services obligation, which in turn tells the collector which ministry's consultation feed to watch.

source_name: eUprava / eParticipacija — Javne rasprave, konsultacije i radne grupe
why_relevant: The national e-government participation module where public consultations, konsultacije, radne grupe and javna obavještenja are centrally listed. Ministry of Finance consultation notices state the draft is available 'na sajtu Ministarstva finansija i portalu e-uprave', so this is the cross-ministry index that catches consultations a single ministry feed might miss.

source_name: Poslovnik Vlade Crne Gore i Poslovnik Skupštine Crne Gore (procedural rulebooks)
why_relevant: Not news, but the schema for everything else: these rulebooks define the mandatory stages (nacrt -> javna rasprava -> izjava/tabela usklađenosti -> utvrđivanje na Vladi -> prvo/drugo čitanje -> amandmani -> usvajanje -> objavljivanje), the minimum consultation durations and the documents that must accompany each bill. Encoding them lets the pipeline predict what artefact should exist next and detect when one is missing.

source_name: Zakon o objavljivanju propisa i drugih akata (publication law)
why_relevant: Defines what must be published in Službeni list Crne Gore, in what form, and the vacatio legis rule that fixes entry into force. Reference text for correctly computing 'stupa na snagu osmog dana od dana objavljivanja' and for asserting a legal publication obligation on any act the collector expects but cannot find.

source_name: Parlamentarna budžetska kancelarija (PBK) — Skupština Crne Gore
why_relevant: Parliament's own budget office produces independent analyses of fiscal and budget bills (e.g. 'Vodič kroz budžet Crne Gore za 2026'). Useful for understanding fiscal-rule legislation (Zakon o budžetu i fiskalnoj odgovornosti) that shapes the banking sector's sovereign exposure and the state's financing needs.

source_name: Bankar.me — Montenegrin banking trade press (legislative pipeline reporting)
why_relevant: Specialist banking outlet that reports on pending legislation with operational framing — e.g. that instant payments readiness was waiting on the adoption of the payments law. Valuable as an early-warning and interpretation layer that names which bill blocks which market capability, and as a discovery channel for bills not yet visible on institutional feeds.

source_name: Montenegrin general business/economy press as bill-stage signal (CdM, Investitor, Mina, Portal Analitika, Standard, Aktuelno)
why_relevant: These outlets consistently report the moment a bill is opened for consultation, sent to committee or adopted, sometimes ahead of the institutional page being indexed — observed for the payments law consultation, fiscal rules and the new Fiskalni savjet. Also flags gaps (e.g. reporting that Montenegro still has no crypto-asset law and MiCA alignment is pending).

source_name: Big-4 / law firm Montenegro regulatory alerts (e.g. KPMG Montenegro tax & legal insights)
why_relevant: Professional-services alerts summarise Montenegrin draft laws in English within days of publication, sometimes attaching the draft PDF itself (observed for the Nacrt Zakona o solidarnom doprinosu). Useful bilingual bridge and a check that the collector has not missed a bill, though always secondary to the official text.

source_name: NVO / civil-society legislative-transparency watchdogs (Akcija za socijalnu pravdu, Institut alternativa, ODIHR opinions)
why_relevant: Reveals indirectly: these actors document where the law-making pipeline fails to publish what it must — notably campaigning for tabele usklađenosti to be published, and ODIHR's opinion on the Montenegrin legislative process (use of urgent procedure, skipped consultations). Essential for calibrating how much of the pipeline is actually observable and for spotting bills pushed through by skraćeni/hitni postupak.

source_name: ILO NATLEX / N-Lex — international mirrors of Montenegrin legislation
why_relevant: International legal-information gateways that index national gazette texts and describe how to query the national collection. Value is as a fallback pointer and English-language entry point when the national gazette site is bot-defended; coverage of financial-sector law is partial and often lagged.

source_name: Narodna banka Srbije — Propisi / Odluke (banking regulation and supervisory decisions)
source_subtype: national central bank / supervisor regulation portal
why_relevant: Serbia is the largest regional home/host jurisdiction adjacent to Montenegro; Serbian-owned or Serbia-domiciled groups (e.g. AIK/Agri Europe cluster, Serbian bidders for Montenegrin banks) are supervised here. NBS regulatory changes on payments, IPS instant payments, capital and consumer protection are frequently copied or anticipated by CBCG, and Serbian bidders for Montenegrin bank stakes require NBS clearance before/alongside CBCG approval.

source_name: Hrvatska narodna banka (HNB) — Supervizija / Regulativa
why_relevant: Croatia is the euro-area/SSM member closest to Montenegro linguistically and commercially; HNB's transposition of EU banking and payments law (Zakon o platnom prometu, CRR/CRD, PSD2/PSD3 prep) is a leading indicator of what Montenegro will adopt during EU accession alignment. Croatian-language texts are directly readable by Montenegrin practitioners and often reused in CBCG drafting.

source_name: Agencija za bankarstvo Federacije BiH (FBA)
why_relevant: FBA publishes laws, subordinate regulations, reporting frameworks and a 'regulations in preparation' section — a rare pre-consultation window. Several groups present in Montenegro (ASA/ASA-Addiko cluster, Intesa, UniCredit, ProCredit, Sparkasse) also hold FBiH subsidiaries, so FBA supervisory actions reveal group-level pressure before it surfaces in Podgorica.

source_name: Agencija za bankarstvo Republike Srpske (ABRS)
why_relevant: The second BiH entity supervisor; a signatory of the EBA Memorandum of Cooperation alongside Montenegro. Its regulation set and enforcement actions are a comparator for CBCG and cover banks with cross-border exposure to Montenegro.

source_name: Centralna banka Bosne i Hercegovine (CBBH)
why_relevant: CBBH coordinates the two entity banking agencies and runs BiH payment systems; useful for regional payment-infrastructure and SEPA-alignment signals and for cross-border financial-stability reporting that includes Montenegro comparators.

source_name: NLB Group — Investor Relations / Investor News
why_relevant: NLB is the parent of NLB Banka Podgorica and the largest SEE-headquartered group. Its regulated disclosures carry group capital requirements (SREP), MREL, resolution planning and M&A that bind the Montenegrin subsidiary — including the 2026 voluntary public takeover offer for Addiko Bank AG, which would reshape ownership across the Western Balkans. Group disclosure typically precedes any CBCG announcement.

source_name: SEOnet — Ljubljana Stock Exchange regulated-information portal
why_relevant: Statutory filing venue where NLB d.d. publishes inside information and general-meeting convocations. Filing here is the legally authoritative, earliest timestamp for group decisions that flow down to NLB Banka Podgorica.
